identity.description: The leaderboard FLOOR for classification: predicts from the class marginals of y alone (most-frequent / prior / stratified / uniform / constant) and never reads a single feature. Its entire purpose is to define the score any real model must beat — a candidate that cannot clear this floor has learned nothing from the features.

consumes.note: X is accepted for API symmetry and IGNORED — only n_samples is read, values are never inspected; the fit consumes y alone (its class marginals)

emits.note: the same label (or a marginal-distributed draw, under stratified/uniform) for every row

predict_proba is strategy-dependent: 'prior' returns the class_prior_ per row; 'most_frequent' a hard one-hot on the majority; 'uniform' flat 1/n_classes; 'stratified' a fresh random draw per row. The prior_brier calibration claim holds ONLY under strategy='prior'.

learnsVsFixed.note: strategy-dependent, and deliberately so: most_frequent/prior/stratified DO fit — they estimate the class marginals from y (the smallest possible fit); constant/uniform learn nothing and are fully specified by their hyperparameters. The component therefore serves both as a trainable floor (refit per leaderboard) and as a fixed reusable reference — hence reusability 'both' even with learns:true

strategy.note: NOT searched on principle — the floor must be a fixed reference; tuning the baseline would move the goalpost every other model is judged against

random_state.note: consulted only by the stochastic strategies (stratified/uniform); pinned so the floor is reproducible

constant.note: the label to always predict when strategy='constant'; must exist in y

invariances.why: predictions are a function of the class marginals of y alone; X never enters the decision, so no rescaling of features can change anything
trivially: X is never read, so ANY transform of the features — monotone or not — leaves predictions bit-identical
missing values in X are irrelevant because feature values are never inspected; only the row count is used
raw string categoricals pass through untouched for the same reason — no encoding is ever consulted
assumes nothing about X (unread); the only implicit claim is that the class marginal is stationary between train and score time — an assumption every supervised model shares
the only estimate is k class frequencies — the lowest-variance fit possible; a handful of rows suffices and cost is a single O(n) count
there is nothing to extend: predictions never depended on X, so outside the training range the output is the same constant prior — constant, not extrapolated

featureStats.why: the dummy's score IS the base rate — most_frequent accuracy equals the majority-class share, so this one number states the floor every other model on the leaderboard is judged against

modelMetrics.why: the Brier score of predicting the marginal for every row — perfectly calibrated, zero resolution; the reference term that decomposes any candidate's Brier into calibration vs discrimination
the whole reason this model exists: every leaderboard entry is read relative to this floor, and a gap near zero means the features carry no usable signal for this target

edgeCases.behavior: predicts that class with probability 1.0 and every candidate ties the floor — the problem itself is degenerate

edgeCases.condition: strategy='constant' with a label absent from y

edgeCases.behavior: most_frequent accuracy approaches 1.0, making raw accuracy meaningless as a scoreboard
edgeCases.note: the floor making this visible is its job — switch the leaderboard metric to PR-AUC / balanced accuracy

placementClaims.why: X is never read; imputation cannot change a prediction derived solely from the class marginals of y
no transform of unread features can alter the output — the fit and predict paths touch only y and n_samples
the scale of features that never enter the decision is immaterial by construction
even raw string categoricals pass through — the estimator inspects only the row count, never a feature value
